answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying influence to a history of useful work, not to free accounts. A new identity starts with zero trust and must earn attested contributions over a long horizon before it can vote or claim rewards, so clones gain nothing at once. Each contribution is signed with a cipher key linked to that history, so clones are easy to spot. Like a glacier, reputation builds slowly through sustained service and melts fast on misbehavior, so an attacker must pay the full time and compute cost for every identity, turning a Sybil flood into a linear, expensive grind.
